page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals average multi-core performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1312.09, placing it in the bottom 25%, while the multi-core CPU test reaches 6986.33, which is in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average throughput, with read-only small block cached speeds at 390.01 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 36.78 GB/sec. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression at 22.7 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 8.79 GB/sec fall into the lower performance tier, whereas database operations and Redis SET operations at 6.6 million operations per second maintain average performance levels.

The instance offers dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent compute resources without virtualization steal, which supports predictable execution for multi-threaded workloads. However, the lack of bundled local storage and a relatively low baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps represent key architectural tradeoffs. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core capabilities, this instance is suited for compute-focused workloads such as multi-threaded batch processing, moderate database operations, and basic web serving that do not require high single-core speeds or local NVMe storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 server provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities, contrasted by weaker single-core and single-threaded compression performance. The instance achieves 6.6 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and an average PassMark CPU score of 8224.85. Lacking local storage, it relies entirely on network-attached volumes. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, moderate database operations, and distributed compute tasks where dedicated CPU allocation is required but massive memory or high single-core throughput is not critical.
